From the field notebook

Not every world
belongs to an orbit.

Iona is an imagined moon with somewhere else to be. This station exists for the brief moment our paths cross.

Stay a little. Look a little closer.
I.
A world in motion

Follow the passage from the first sighting to the last trace. Iona grows closer, meets the reference line, then recedes into the western dark.

One moon. Three moments.

Your point of view

Drag the sky or change the telescope bearing. At alignment, center your view to bring Iona and the guide stars into a shared reference.

Observer’s guide
×
Make a little space
for the sky.
Follow the passage.

Move the passage slider, or choose Arrival, Alignment, and Departure. The moon’s position, distance, and trail change with you.

Steer your telescope.

Drag horizontally across the sky or use Telescope bearing. At Alignment, choose Center to match the station’s reference line.

Set your own pace.

Nothing advances without you. Turn motion off for immediate scene changes. Your device’s reduced-motion setting is respected automatically.

Using a keyboard? Tab to a slider and use the arrow keys. Every stage also has its own button.
